definitions.explanation: To put plants, seeds, or trees into the ground so they can grow. The transitive act of cultivation.
Figuratively, to implant ideas, values, or attitudes in someone's mind.

examples.english: I planted flowers in the garden.
examples.notes: に marks the location, を marks what is planted

examples.english: I plant vegetable seeds in spring.
I planted a cherry tree in the park.

notes:
TRANSITIVITY: {他動詞|たどうし} (transitive). No common intransitive pair. Pattern: Xに Yを{植|う}える (plant Y in/at X).

ASPECT: ている indicates resulting state. {植|う}えてある = 'has been planted' (resultative, focus on the state); {植|う}えている = 'is planting' (progressive) or 'has planted.'

COMMON PATTERNS:
・{木|き}を{植|う}える (plant a tree)
・{花|はな}を{植|う}える (plant flowers)
・{種|たね}を{植|う}える (plant seeds)
・{庭|にわ}に{植|う}える (plant in the garden)
・{田植|たう}え (rice planting—noun form)

COMPOUND VERBS:
・{植|う}えつける (to implant firmly)
・{植|う}え{替|か}える (to transplant)

HOMOPHONE: Don't confuse with {飢|う}える (to starve), which is pronounced the same but written differently.
